agent: wave 15 agent B - the five collectors: what the weighted walk is actually for
question: What the slot-10 trigger walk collects and keyed by what; why five collector entry points rather than one and what 0x4A51C0's text argument is for; what reads the collection and when; and whether the five are really five.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::AddConquerProv
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CAIStrategy::AddConquerProv(CAIStrategy* this@ESI, int province_id@stack:0x4, int weight@stack:0x8)
addresses.comment:
**The first of the ten weighted list adders on CAIStrategy, and one of the five the trigger walk reaches.** 0x4A4F50 to the `ret 8` at 0x4A508B; ten `int3` above it and two below. The receiver arrives in **ESI** - the body never writes esi - so it is a compiler-chosen register convention and not a `__thiscall`.

    state = get_or_create(g_CCurrentGameState)                       ; 0x4A4F69, the 0xDA8 allocation
    if (state->provinces_begin[province_id]->owner_id == this->tag.id) return   ; 0x4A4FF0-0x4A5002
    if (weight) AIStrategyList_AddProvinceWeight(&this->conquer_prov, province_id, weight)
    cap = (this->Personality == _AI_MILITARIST_) ? 0x3C : 0x28       ; 0x4A5016-0x4A5023
    while (this->conquer_prov_count > cap) pop the tail and delete its CProvinceValue

So a condition that argues for a province adds its weight to `conquer_prov`, **except for a province the strategy's own country already owns**, and the list is then trimmed from the **low-weight end** to 40 entries, or 60 for a militarist AI. `CMapProvince +0x330` is `owner_id` and `CEventScope +0x28` is `province`, both already recorded, which is what fixes the first argument as a province id.

Five callers: MergeAIStrategy (0x4A3BCF), 0x4A6957, and three leaf slot-10 bodies - `CControlsTrigger`/`COwnsTrigger` (0x5D5F4E), `COwnedByTrigger` (0x5DF92E) and `CFactionTrigger` (0x5FCB7F). The trigger side passes `scope->province` and the walk's weight.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A4F50-0x4A508B end to end from the entry; functionStart lands on it exactly and retsBefore is empty. The province indexing is `state->+0xB8C`, which the record already names `provinces_begin`, and `+0x330`, which it already names `owner_id`. The caps are immediates (0x28/0x3C) tested against `+0x18`, which the record already names `Personality`; the enum value 1 = militarist is independently confirmed by PersonalityTokenToEnum (rva 0x4A4080) mapping save token 0x39F (`military`) to 1. The savegame is the oracle: in Ireland1942_05_11_11.hoi3 the largest `conquer_prov` block is 38 entries, under both caps. Would be shown wrong by a `conquer_prov` block of more than 60 entries in any save, or by the receiver turning out to be loaded rather than incoming in ESI.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::AddDefendProv
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CAIStrategy::AddDefendProv(CAIStrategy* this@ESI, int province_id@stack:0x4, int weight@stack:0x8)
addresses.comment:
**The `defend_prov` adder**, the same shape as CAIStrategy::AddConquerProv (0x4A4F50) with two differences: the list is `defend_prov` at `+0x2C` (`lea eax,[esi+0x2c]` at 0x4A514C) and the cap is a flat **1000** (`cmp [esi+0x34], 0x3e8` at 0x4A5156 and 0x4A51A4), with no Personality test. 0x4A5090 to the `ret 8` at 0x4A51BC, receiver in ESI.

Three callers and **none of them is a trigger**: MergeAIStrategy (0x4A3BF1), 0x4A69B5 and 0x4A6A93. So `defend_prov` is filled by the AI itself rather than by the trigger walk.

Abutment note: it ends `ret 8` at 0x4A51BC with a **single `int3`** before CAIStrategy::AddBuildingProv at 0x4A51C0 - trap 2's shape, although `functionStart` happens to get it right here because the next function opens `push ebp`.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry; the two `cmp ... 0x3e8` sites and the `lea [esi+0x2c]` read directly, and `+0x2C` is `defend_prov` in both project.json and BiceLib/GameClasses/CAIStrategy.hpp. findRefs --callers gives exactly three call sites, none in the trigger region. The save's largest `defend_prov` block is 183 entries - consistent with a cap of 1000 and inconsistent with 40 or 60. Would be shown wrong by a trigger-region caller, or by a `defend_prov` block over 1000 entries.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::AddBuildingProv
addresses.no_signature: A compiler-chosen register convention with a by-value string in the middle of it. Two stack arguments - the CAIStrategy at [ebp+8] and a `Hoi3CString` **by value** at [ebp+0xC], 0x1C bytes, hence `ret 0x20` - plus the province id in **EDX** and the weight in **ECX**. It then forwards EDX and ECX by pushing them in its own prologue (`push ecx; push ecx; push edx` at 0x4A51D8) so that they land as AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight's arguments 3 and 4: the register arguments are passed on by stack position, not by register. No ordinary signature expresses that without inventing stack parameters the `ret` would then disagree with.
addresses.comment:
**The one collector handed text, and the only one the trigger walk reaches that is not a weight on an id.** 0x4A51C0 to the `ret 0x20` at 0x4A522E, 0x11 `int3` below it.

    local = Hoi3CString(name)                                   ; copy the by-value argument
    AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight(&strategy->building_prov,  ; 0x4A5203: +0x10C
                                     local, province@EDX, weight@ECX)

So **the text is a building name and the list is `building_prov` at `+0x10C`**, whose element is a `CStringIntInt`: province id at `+8`, the building name at `+0xC`, accumulated weight at `+0x28`. That is why this one is shaped differently - it is the only list in the family keyed by a **pair**, and the pair's second half is a name rather than an id, so the generic province adder cannot serve it.

One caller in the whole image: the call at 0x5E4AA2 in `CHasBuildingTrigger::WalkChildren`. That leaf reads `*(this->+0x40) + 0x1C` as the name - the building definition's own name string, not a copy held on the trigger - puts `scope->province` in EDX and the walk's weight in ECX. MergeAIStrategy does **not** come through here: it calls AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight (0x4A58F0) directly at 0x4A3C6C, having built the string itself. So this body exists purely to adapt the trigger leaf's call shape.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A51C0-0x4A522E and 0x5E4A50-0x5E4AAB end to end. The 0x20 of callee cleanup decomposes exactly as 4 (the strategy) + 0x1C (`Hoi3CString`, whose size the record declares), and 0x4A58F0's own `ret 0x28` = 4 + 0x1C + 4 + 4 confirms the two extra dwords are arguments of the callee rather than locals of this function. `+0x10C` is `building_prov` in both project.json and CAIStrategy.hpp. The payload class is CStringIntInt, read off the vftable the constructor at 0x4A32B0 writes (VA 0x15EBF08, rva 0x11EBF08) and resolved against the RTTI export. findRefs --callers gives exactly one caller. Would be shown wrong by a second caller, or by 0x4A58F0's `ret` not being 0x28.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::AddThreat
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CAIStrategy::AddThreat(CAIStrategy* this@EAX, int weight@stack:0x4, int tag_chars@stack:0x8, int country_id@stack:0xC)
addresses.comment:
**The `threat` adder, and the thinnest member of the family**: the whole of 0x4A5240-0x4A525F is a forward to AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight (0x4A5A60) with the list at `+0x3C` and its hash at `+0x4C`, and **no trim at all** - `threat` is the one uncapped list of the ten. The receiver arrives in **EAX** and is passed straight through, which is the convention 0x4A5A60 itself wants.

One caller, 0x4A7390, and it is **not** a trigger: MergeAIStrategy calls 0x4A5A60 directly at 0x4A3CC8. `threat` is therefore not fed by the trigger walk at all, which is worth knowing because it is the list the record already has a reader for - CAIUnit::SetArea indexes `threat` by country id through `+0x50`/`+0x54`.
addresses.evidence: Eight instructions, decoded whole: `lea edx,[eax+0x4c]` and `lea ecx,[eax+0x3c]` are the only two addresses it forms, and the three stack dwords it pushes are its own [ebp+8], [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10] in that order, which land as 0x4A5A60's weight/tag_chars/country_id. `ret 0xC` matches three stack arguments with the receiver in a register. findRefs --callers gives one caller. Would be shown wrong by the receiver being loaded from the stack somewhere in those eight instructions, which it is not.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::AddAntagonize
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CAIStrategy::AddAntagonize(CAIStrategy* this@stack:0x4, int tag_chars@stack:0x8, int country_id@stack:0xC, int weight@EDX)
addresses.comment:
**The `antagonize` adder** - the collector the record previously described only as 'inserting into a map a CAIStrategy owns'. 0x4A5270 to the `ret 0xC` at 0x4A533C.

    AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight(&this->antagonize /*+0x58*/, &this->antagonize_hash /*+0x68*/,
                                   weight@EDX, tag_chars, country_id, this@EAX)
    while (this->antagonize_count /*+0x60*/ > 7) pop the tail and delete its CCountryValue

So the key is a **country** - tag letters and id, the two halves of a CCountryTag - the value is an accumulated weight, and the list is trimmed from the low-weight end to **7** entries.

Ten callers, six of them trigger leaves: MergeAIStrategy (0x4A3CF1), 0x4A77C8, 0x4A7F60, `CExistsTrigger` (0x5DABD0), `CRelationTrigger` on the polarity-set branch (0x5DF181), `CUndeclaredWarWithTrigger`/`CWarWithTrigger` (0x5EB089), `CVassalOfTrigger` (0x5EF54D, 0x5EF57A), `CAllianceWithTrigger` (0x5EFC05) and `CFactionTrigger` (0x5FCB99).

Abutment note: `ret 0xc` at 0x4A533C with a **single `int3`** before CAIStrategy::AddRival at 0x4A5340.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A5270-0x4A533C from the entry. The two `lea`s give the list and hash bases, which agree with CAIStrategy's existing `antagonize` at +0x58 and `antagonize_bucket_count`/`antagonize_buckets` at +0x6C/+0x70 - the hash base is list+0x10 and the recorded pair is hash+4/hash+8. `cmp [esi+0x60], 7` is the cap, read as an immediate. The savegame is the oracle: the largest `antagonize` block in Ireland1942_05_11_11.hoi3 is **exactly 7**. Would be shown wrong by an 8-entry `antagonize` block in any save.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::AddBefriend
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CAIStrategy::AddBefriend(CAIStrategy* this@stack:0x4, int tag_chars@stack:0x8, int country_id@stack:0xC, int weight@EDX)
addresses.comment:
**The `befriend` adder, and the other half of CRelationTrigger's polarity switch.** 0x4A5420 to the `ret 0xC` at 0x4A550F. List at `+0x74`, hash at `+0x84`, and the cap is **Personality-dependent**: `if (this->Personality == _AI_DIPLOMAT_) cap = 0xE else cap = 7` (0x4A5447-0x4A5454).

Six callers, four of them trigger leaves: MergeAIStrategy (0x4A3D15), 0x4A8AB5, `CRelationTrigger` on the polarity-clear branch (0x5DF19A), `CVassalOfTrigger` (0x5EF55F, 0x5EF58A) and `CAllianceWithTrigger` (0x5EFBF7). This is what `CRelationTrigger::WalkChildren` switches between: 0x4A5270 (`antagonize`) when the flag is set, this (`befriend`) when it is clear - so a `relation` condition under an odd number of NOTs argues for antagonising and under an even number for courting.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry. `+0x74` is `befriend` in project.json and CAIStrategy.hpp. The cap test is `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x18], 3` against the Personality field, and 3 is `_AI_DIPLOMAT_` in the generated AIPersonality enum - independently confirmed by PersonalityTokenToEnum (rva 0x4A4080) mapping save token 0x2A4 (`diplomacy`) to 3. The savegame is the oracle: the largest `befriend` block in Ireland1942_05_11_11.hoi3 is **exactly 14**, which only the diplomat branch allows. Would be shown wrong by a 15-entry `befriend` block.

addresses.name: AIStrategyList_AddProvinceWeight
addresses.signature: void __stdcall AIStrategyList_AddProvinceWeight(CList<CProvinceValue*>* list, int province_id, int weight)
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A5800-0x4A58EB end to end. The payload is `operator new(0x10)` with `[eax+4] = 0x18D`, `[eax] = 0x15EBEEC`, `[eax+8] = key`, `[eax+0xC] = weight` at 0x4A5861-0x4A5885, and VA 0x15EBEEC resolves to CProvinceValue in the RTTI export (trap 1: the export prints VAs, so the rva is 0x11EBEEC). The `jle` at 0x4A5890 on the accumulated value is what decides delete against insert. The unlink helper is at VA 0x5D49D0, i.e. **rva 0x1D49D0** - note that CDiplomacyStatus::ClearCasusBelli's comment in project.json calls the same function `0x5D49D0`, which read as an rva points at a byte in the middle of another function; `image.read` at VA 0x9D49D0 is `push eax; mov fs:[0],...` and at VA 0x5D49D0 is a clean `push ebp; mov ebp,esp; mov eax,[ebp+8]`. The sort direction comes from 0x4AE630, read separately. Would be shown wrong by 0x4AE630 turning out to insert at a fixed end rather than by comparison.

addresses.name: AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight
addresses.signature: void __stdcall AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight(CList<CStringIntInt*>* list, Hoi3CString building, int province_id, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**The building_prov insert - the same accumulate-and-resort as AIStrategyList_AddProvinceWeight, but matching on a pair.** 0x4A58F0 to the `ret 0x28` at 0x4A5A5A, which decomposes as 4 + 0x1C (the `Hoi3CString` by value) + 4 + 4.

An existing element matches only when **both** `CStringIntInt->id == province_id` and its `key` string compares equal (0x4A593D for the id, the `std::string` compare at rva 0x15F70 for the name), and then `[payload+0x28] += weight`. A new one is `operator new(0x2C)` through the constructor at 0x4A32B0, which writes vftable rva 0x11EBF08 and stores the string at `+0xC` and the id at `+8`. The re-insert goes through 0x4AE700 rather than 0x4AE630 - the same sorted insert on `+0x28` instead of `+0xC`, because this payload keeps its weight at a different offset.

Two callers: MergeAIStrategy (0x4A3C6C), which builds the string itself, and CAIStrategy::AddBuildingProv (0x4A520A), which is the trigger side's adapter.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A58F0-0x4A5A5A. The 0x2C allocation and the constructor at 0x4A32B0 were read in full; VA 0x15EBF08 resolves to CStringIntInt in the RTTI export, whose RTTI base is CPersistent at offset 0 and whose slot 2 is the `SaveContents` at rva 0x76DE0 that writes `key` (save token 0xE5), `id` (0xB) and `value` (0x2A6) out of +0xC, +8 and +0x28 - three independent agreements on the layout. Would be shown wrong by the `ret` not being 0x28, or by rva 0x15F70 not being a string comparison.

addresses.name: AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight
addresses.signature: void __stdcall AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight(CList<CCountryValue*>* list@stack:0x4, void* hash@stack:0x8, int weight@stack:0xC, int tag_chars@stack:0x10, int country_id@stack:0x14, CAIStrategy* strategy@EAX)
addresses.comment:
**The country-keyed weighted insert - the shared body behind seven of the ten adders.** 0x4A5A60 to two `ret 0x14` exits at 0x4A5B19 and 0x4A5B3E. Five stack arguments and the strategy in **EAX**.

    if (country_id == strategy->tag.id) return            ; 0x4A5A6C - never record yourself
    if (!weight) return
    bucket = hash->buckets[country_id % hash->bucket_count]
    node = the bucket chain entry whose CCountryValue->tag.id == country_id
    if (node) {
        node->value += weight
        CList_RemoveNode(list, <its list element>)        ; rva 0x1D49D0
        if (node->value < 1) { CountryHash_Remove(hash, node); delete node; return }
    } else {
        if (weight <= 0) return
        node = new CCountryValue(tag_chars, country_id, weight)   ; operator new(0x14), vftable rva 0x11EBEB4
        CountryHash_Insert(hash, node)                    ; 0x4AE580
    }
    CountryList_InsertByWeight(list, &node)               ; 0x4DD670

So the seven country-keyed lists are each a **list plus a hash over the same payloads** - the list for ordered, capped iteration and the hash for `strategy->threat[countryId]`-style lookup, which is what CAIUnit::SetArea already uses. The hash sub-object sits at **list + 0x10** in every one of the seven and is `{count, bucket_count, buckets}`, with `bucket_count` 0x1FF.

Eight callers: MergeAIStrategy (0x4A3CC8) and the seven adders (0x4A5258, 0x4A528C, 0x4A5362, 0x4A5442, 0x4A5545, 0x4A5642, 0x4A5722).
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A5A60-0x4A5B3E end to end. `div dword ptr [esi+4]` and `[esi+8]` fix bucket_count and buckets at hash+4 and hash+8; `inc dword ptr [esi]` in the insert helper 0x4AE580 fixes the element count at hash+0. The payload is `operator new(0x14)` with vftable VA 0x15EBEB4 (rva 0x11EBEB4) = CCountryValue in the RTTI export, tag chars at +8, id at +0xC, value at +0x10, which `CCountryValue::SaveContents` (rva 0x764C0) corroborates by writing `id` from +8 as a string and `value` from +0x10. The seven callers each pass list and list+0x10, and two of the seven pairs (+0x3C/+0x4C and +0x58/+0x68) agree with bucket fields already in project.json at +0x50/+0x54 and +0x6C/+0x70. Would be shown wrong by one of the seven passing a hash base other than list+0x10, which none does.

addresses.name: AIStrategyList_InsertByWeight
addresses.comment:
**Sorted insert, descending by the payload's `+0xC`** - what keeps `conquer_prov` and `defend_prov` ranked so that their caller's trim from the tail drops the weakest entries. 0x4AE630 to the `ret 8` at 0x4AE66A and a second exit below it.

It walks from `list->last` backwards along `node->prev`, stopping at the first node whose `data->+0xC` is **>=** the new value, and links the new node after it; if the walk reaches the head without finding one, the value is the largest and it goes to the front through rva 0x5F5E0. The node it builds is the ordinary CList node - `{data, prev, next, flag}` at +0/+4/+8/+0xC - and it bumps `list->count`.

Its siblings 0x4AE700 and 0x4DD670 do the same thing on `+0x28` and `+0x10`, for the CStringIntInt and CCountryValue payloads.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4AE630-0x4AE6B2. `mov esi,[ecx+4]` starts at list+4, `mov edi,[edi+4]` walks, and `cmp [edx+0xc], eax; jge` is the comparison - so the order is high-to-low from head to tail. The node field order it writes (`[eax]=data, [eax+4]=prev, [eax+8]=0, [eax+0xC]=0`) matches the generated `CListNode<T>` the record already carries. Would be shown wrong by the comparison being `jle`, or by list+4 being `first` rather than `last` - which the trim loops in the ten adders settle independently, since they pop list+4 and follow +4.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::ClearCollectedLists
addresses.comment:
**What makes every CAIStrategy::Rebuild a from-scratch rebuild rather than an accumulation.** 0x4A3DE0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4A4075; twelve `int3` above it. The receiver arrives in **EDI**.

The first 0x1F0 bytes empty all ten collected lists and all seven of their hashes, and they are the whole family's offsets in one place - 17 `lea`s in order: `+0x1C` (conquer_prov), `+0x2C` (defend_prov), `+0x10C` (building_prov), then `+0x4C`/`+0x3C` (threat), `+0x68`/`+0x58` (antagonize), `+0x84`/`+0x74` (befriend), `+0xA0`/`+0x90` (protect), `+0x12C`/`+0x11C` (rival), `+0xBC`/`+0xAC` (vassal), `+0xD8`/`+0xC8` (military_access). List clears go through rva 0xB6260 and hash clears through rva 0x93940.

From 0x4A3ECE there is a **tail this reading stopped at**: it get-or-creates a 0xC0-byte singleton at the absolute 0x1A886F0, with a 0x1FF-bucket hash of its own at its +0x14/+0x18, and walks the vector at its +0x1C/+0x20; part of that is gated on the `bool` at `[ebp+8]`, tested at 0x4A3FD1. CAIStrategy::Rebuild passes 0; the other four callers (0xCA84E, 0xD3D9F, 0xD3DAC, 0x4A38B0) were not checked. That tail is AI-side, and it is why this entry is `inferred` rather than `confirmed`: the name describes two thirds of the body.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A3DE0-0x4A4075. The 17 `lea [edi+N]` sites were listed mechanically and every one of the ten list offsets matches a field project.json and CAIStrategy.hpp already name, with the seven hash bases exactly list+0x10 - the same pairing the seven adders pass to 0x4A5A60, reached by a different route. `ret 4` against one stack argument and a register receiver. Marked inferred because the tail from 0x4A3ECE was not read and could do something the name does not cover. Would be shown wrong by that tail writing back into the ten lists.

addresses.name: PersonalityTokenToEnum
addresses.comment:
**The whole of the `personality` key's parse, and the thing that makes the collectors' caps readable.** 0x4A4080 to the last of four bare `ret`s at 0x4A40AE; fifteen instructions, no frame, the token in EAX and the answer in EAX.

    military  (token 0x39F) -> 1   _AI_MILITARIST_
    capital   (token 0x1F9) -> 2   _AI_INDUSTRIALIST_
    diplomacy (token 0x2A4) -> 3   _AI_DIPLOMAT_
    anything else           -> 4   _AI_BALANCED_

That settles the two Personality-dependent caps in the collector family off the game's own loader rather than off the Lua enum alone: `conquer_prov` holds 60 instead of 40 for a **militarist** AI (CAIStrategy::AddConquerProv), and `befriend` and `protect` hold 14 instead of 7 for a **diplomat** (CAIStrategy::AddBefriend, CAIStrategy::AddProtect). One caller, 0x4A42D7, inside CAIStrategy::LoadKey.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole - three `cmp` immediates and four `mov eax,N; ret`. The three tokens resolve in ghidra/saveTokens.json to `military`, `capital` and `diplomacy`, and the four results are exactly values 1-4 of the generated CAIStrategy::AIPersonality enum, whose names are _AI_MILITARIST_, _AI_INDUSTRIALIST_, _AI_DIPLOMAT_ and _AI_BALANCED_ in that order. A savegame cross-checks it: Germany's `ai` block in Ireland1942_05_11_11.hoi3 reads `personality=military` and its `conquer_prov` list is 38 long, which only the 60 cap allows. Would be shown wrong by the enum's order differing from the Lua registration it comes from.

addresses.name: MergeAIStrategy
addresses.revises: The entry said 'What it does with the 18 fields was not read.' It is now read: the body is a call to each of the ten weighted list adders in turn, which is what identifies them as a family and is what makes the trigger walk's five a subset rather than the whole of it. The extent is added. Nothing the entry already claimed is changed, and its `likely` is kept. The entry's confidence reads `inferred` only because the merge validator has no `likely`; the strength is unchanged from the `likely` project.json already held.
addresses.comment:
Folds one CAIStrategy into an accumulator. 0x4A3B90 to the `ret 8` at 0x4A3DD1. Three call sites and they are the whole story of how AI strategy reaches the AI: ApplyCountryAIStrategies passes `CCountry+0x1DC` (`ai_hard_strategy`) and `CCountry+0x334` (`ai_event_strategy`), and CAddAIStrategyEffect::Execute (0x5B0E00) passes the effect's own embedded CAIStrategy. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ai.md.

*(2026-10-01: both arguments retyped. The first was `AIStrategyCache*`, which is not a declared struct. The second was `CAIStrategy**`; it is one level of indirection too many, and the bytes say so - `mov eax, [ebp+0xc]` at 0x4A3BA1 is followed directly by `mov edi, [eax+0x1c]` at 0x4A3BB4, a field read with no load in between, and `+0x1c` is then walked as a list head (`[edi]` to the node's data, `[edi+8]` to the next node). A `CAIStrategy**` would have had to be dereferenced first. Checked here because the survey and the record disagreed.)*

**What it does with the lists, added 2026-10-06.** It walks each of `src`'s ten collected lists and re-adds every entry into `dest` through that list's own weighted adder, so merging two strategies *sums* their weights entry by entry rather than concatenating them. The ten calls, in body order: 0x4A3BCF CAIStrategy::AddConquerProv, 0x4A3BF1 AddDefendProv, 0x4A3C6C AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight (building_prov, reached directly - it builds the `Hoi3CString` itself at 0x4A3C32/0x4A3C60 rather than going through AddBuildingProv), 0x4A3CC8 AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight (threat, also direct), 0x4A3CF1 AddAntagonize, 0x4A3D15 AddBefriend, 0x4A3D41 AddProtect, 0x4A3D68 AddRival, 0x4A3D91 AddVassal, 0x4A3DB8 AddMilitaryAccess. **That is the complete set of ten and the reason the adders are a family**: five of them are also reached from trigger slot-10 leaves and five are not.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4A3B90-0x4A3DD1 and listed every `call` in it; the ten adder calls are the only calls besides two `std::string` copies and one free. Each target is one of the ten bodies read in this fragment. Confidence left at the entry's existing `likely` because what it claims beyond this - the retyped arguments and the three call sites - was not re-derived here. Would be shown wrong by an eleventh adder call in the body, or by one of the ten not being where the decode put it.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::Rebuild
addresses.revises: The caller list was recorded as **virtual addresses** while every other address in project.json is an rva (trap 1), so each of the eleven was 0x400000 too high; `0x4DB7C4` read as an rva is not a call site at all. The count was also contradicted by ApplyCountryAIStrategies' entry, which says eight. findRefs gives eleven, and this entry now names the enclosing function of each - which is the answer to how often the trigger slot-10 walk runs, because this is its only route in. The list of callees is also respelled as rvas (it mixed both forms), and the clear-before-rebuild at 0x4A5D15 is added. The entry's confidence reads `inferred` only because the merge validator has no `likely`; the strength is unchanged from the `likely` project.json already held.
addresses.comment:
Rebuilds a country's merged AI strategy. 0x4A5C90 to the bare `ret` at 0x4A5DCD. Bails when `+0xC` is null or the tag at `+8` is `REB`, and also when `country->+0xCF8 <= 0` and when a virtual on `0x2F100()->+0x2B4` answers false; then calls **CAIStrategy::ClearCollectedLists(this, 0)** (0x4A5D15), stamps `+0x10 = gamestate->tick` (0x4A5D99) and finally `+0x14 = 1` (`initialized`), and in between calls 0x4A5DD0, 0x4ACE20, 0x4AD430, ApplyCountryAIStrategies (0x4A62A0) and 0x4AD6E0. Because it clears first, **every rebuild re-derives all ten collected lists from nothing** - the weights in a savegame's `ai` block are one rebuild's worth, not a running total over the game.

**Eleven direct callers, as rvas** (the previous list gave virtual addresses): 0xDB7C4 inside `RunCountryDailyPass` (0xDA530), 0xE055D (in 0xE0460), 0xE3E5E (in 0xE39C0), 0xE6CCB inside `CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies`, 0xEF2A2 and 0xEF781 (both in 0xEE860), 0xF640E and 0xF645B inside `CFaction::AddCountry`, 0x25C282 inside `CInGameIdler::Enter`, 0x5B0E78 inside `CAddAIStrategyEffect::Execute`, and 0x64018C inside `CPeaceAction::Apply`.

**Only the daily one is gated on the stamp**: `RunCountryDailyPass` calls it as `if (!strategy->initialized && !strategy->is_static) Rebuild()` at 0xDB7AF-0xDB7C4, reading `CCountry +0x4A0`, which is `strategy+0x14`. So after the first successful rebuild the daily pass skips it, and the rest are **event-driven** - entering a session, a war's membership changing, a faction joining, a peace, or an `add_ai_strategy` effect firing. The AI's weighted trigger walk is therefore not a periodic cost at all; see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md.

**Renamed 2026-10-01 from `AIStrategyCache::Rebuild`.** `AIStrategyCache` was a good *description* - the object caches the country's two loaded strategies merged together, and the `+0x10 = tick` / `+0x14 = 1` stamp this writes is exactly a cache validity stamp - but it is not a class, and the receiver has a name already: every caller passes `&country[+0x48C]`, which the record declares as `CAIStrategy`. See `FINDINGS-aitheatre.md`.
addresses.evidence: findRefs.py --callers 0x008A5C90 gives eleven sites and prints virtual addresses; converting each gives the rvas above, and the old list is each of those plus 0x400000. The enclosing functions come from functionStart with retsBefore(start, site) == 0 in every case, cross-checked against project.json's recorded rvas for four of them. 0xDAE94, which functionStart answers for the daily site, is **not** an entry - the bytes there are `mov esi,ebx` after `push 0; push ecx; mov ecx,esp`, mid-function - and retsBefore(0xDA530, 0xDB7C4) is 0, which puts the call inside RunCountryDailyPass. The clear-before-rebuild and the tick stamp were decoded at 0x4A5D15 and 0x4A5D92-0x4A5D99. Confidence left at the entry's existing `likely` because the five functions this calls between the clear and the stamp were not read. Would be shown wrong by a twelfth caller, or by RunCountryDailyPass's gate reading something other than strategy+0x14/+0x15.

addresses.name: CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies
addresses.revises: Two address errors in the caller list, and one of them carries a frequency claim. It said '0x65B398 (inside CInGameIdler's hourly body)'; 0x65B398 is a **virtual** address (rva 0x25B398) and functionStart answers CInGameIdler::Enter with retsBefore 0 - so that call is at **session entry**, not hourly. It also said 'eight in the diplomacy action code at 0x4A503D6..0x4A51BF5', which is out of range read either way; the eight are rvas 0x6503D6/0x6503E7 in CWar::AddAttacker, 0x650653/0x650666 in CWar::RemoveAttacker, 0x6516B2/0x6516C3 in CWar::AddDefender and 0x651BE2/0x651BF5 in CWar::RemoveDefender. This matters outside its own entry because this function calls CAIStrategy::Rebuild unconditionally, so 'hourly' here would have made the AI's whole weighted trigger walk an hourly cost. The body addresses in the first paragraph are also respelled as rvas. The entry's confidence reads `inferred` only because the merge validator has no `likely`; the strength is unchanged from the `likely` project.json already held.
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies(CCountry* this, bool allowDemobilise, bool suppressDemobilise)
addresses.comment:
0xE6A70-0xE6ED3, `ret 8`, `this` in ecx. **The only writer of `CCountry +0xACC` (at_war) and of the enemies list at `+0x1008`.** It clears `+0xACC`, frees `+0x1008`/`+0x100C`/`+0x1010`, then walks the whole country database (the singleton at absolute 0x1A855A4, `+0x168` count, `+0x16C` array) and for every other country whose `CDiplomacyStatus +0x20` (war) is non-null: sets `+0xACC = 1`, appends a 0x14-byte `{tagChars, tagId, prev, next, byte}` node to `+0x1008`, and stamps the pair's `CDiplomacyStatus +0x54` with the current tick (`state->+0xBDC`). It then runs the mobilisation side: with `+0x94` clear and `+0xACC` set it adds the static modifier `initial_mobilization` and sets `+0x94 = 1`; the reverse transitions remove it, and the one at 0xE6E44 also clears `+0x94` - but only for a country the played-countries array `state->+0xBCC` says is not played. The name is from the body.

**Nine call sites, as rvas, corrected 2026-10-06.** One is 0x25B398, which is inside **`CInGameIdler::Enter`** (rva 0x25A2B0) and therefore runs once when a session comes up - the entry previously said 'CInGameIdler's hourly body', which was a virtual address read as an rva *and* the wrong function. The other eight are two apiece in `CWar::AddAttacker` (0x6503D6, 0x6503E7), `CWar::RemoveAttacker` (0x650653, 0x650666), `CWar::AddDefender` (0x6516B2, 0x6516C3) and `CWar::RemoveDefender` (0x651BE2, 0x651BF5) - always on **both** sides of the membership change.

It also calls `CAIStrategy::Rebuild` on `this + 0x48C` at 0xE6CCB, gated only on `state->in_game`, so a war's membership changing rebuilds both sides' AI strategy from scratch.
addresses.evidence: findRefs.py --callers 0x004E6A70 gives nine sites, printed as virtual addresses: 0x65B398 and eight in 0xA50000-0xA52000. functionStart on each, with retsBefore(start, site) == 0 throughout, gives CInGameIdler::Enter (rva 0x25A2B0, already recorded) for the first and the four CWar methods (rvas 0x64F220, 0x650440, 0x6506B0, 0x651710, all already recorded) for the eight. The Rebuild call and its `state->+0xDA4` gate were decoded at 0xE6CBB-0xE6CCB. Everything else in the comment is the existing entry's, respelled from VAs to rvas but not re-derived. Would be shown wrong by CInGameIdler::Enter not spanning 0x25B398 - it does: 0x25A2B0 to past 0x25C282, which is this file's own second Rebuild site.

structs.name: CProvinceValue
structs.comment: **A province id with an int against it** - the element of CAIStrategy's `conquer_prov` and `defend_prov` lists. 0x10 bytes: CPersistent's vftable and token at +0 and +4 (the token is always 0x18D), the province id at +8 and the value at +0xC. Its SaveContents (rva 0x76B90) writes `id` and `value`, which is exactly how a `conquer_prov` block reads in a savegame.
structs.evidence: `operator new(0x10)` at 0x4A5861 and 0x4A5896 in AIStrategyList_AddProvinceWeight, writing vftable VA 0x15EBEEC (rva 0x11EBEEC, trap 1) and token 0x18D, the key at +8 and the weight at +0xC. The RTTI export gives the class that vftable and one base, CPersistent at offset 0, and its `introduces` list (which stores VAs) puts SaveContents at VA 0x476B90 and LoadKey at VA 0x476B30, i.e. rvas 0x76B90 and 0x76B30. Two savegames show the `{id,value}` pair. Would be shown wrong by an allocation of this class at a size other than 0x10.

structs.name: CCountryValue
structs.comment: **A country tag with an int against it** - the element of the seven country-keyed CAIStrategy lists (`threat`, `antagonize`, `befriend`, `protect`, `vassal`, `military_access`, `rival`), held in both the list and the hash beside it. 0x14 bytes: CPersistent at +0/+4, a `CCountryTag` by value at +8 (letters at +8, id at +0xC) and the value at +0x10. Its SaveContents (rva 0x764C0) writes `id` from the tag letters and `value` from +0x10, which is how a `threat` or `befriend` block reads in a savegame. The hash beside the list buckets it by `+0xC % 0x1FF`.
structs.evidence: `operator new(0x14)` at 0x4A5AA7 in AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight, writing vftable VA 0x15EBEB4 (rva 0x11EBEB4), token 0x18D, tag letters at +8, id at +0xC and weight at +0x10. The RTTI export gives the class that vftable and CPersistent at offset 0. Independently: CCountryValue::SaveContents (rva 0x764C0) takes `strlen(this+8)` to build the `id` string and reads `this+0x10` for `value`, and the hash insert at 0x4AE580 divides `[payload+0xC]` by the bucket count - three readings of the same three fields by different routes. Would be shown wrong by an allocation at a size other than 0x14.

structs.name: CStringIntInt
structs.comment: **A name, an id and a value** - the element of CAIStrategy's `building_prov`, and the only payload in the collector family keyed by a pair. 0x2C bytes: CPersistent at +0/+4, the id at +8, a `Hoi3CString` at +0xC and the value at +0x28. Its SaveContents (rva 0x76DE0) writes the three under the keys `key` (save token 0xE5), `id` (0xB) and `value` (0x2A6), in that order; the class name is the game's own, out of the RTTI export, and describes the save order rather than the layout.
structs.evidence: `operator new(0x2C)` at 0x4A599D in AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight, constructed by 0x4A32B0, which writes vftable VA 0x15EBF08 (rva 0x11EBF08), token 0x18D, the id at +8 and a fresh Hoi3CString at +0xC; the value at +0x28 is read and written at 0x4A59EC and 0x4A5A04, and 0xC + 0x1C = 0x28 closes the layout with no gap. The RTTI export gives the class that vftable and CPersistent at offset 0, and its SaveContents's three save tokens resolve in ghidra/saveTokens.json to `key`, `id` and `value`. Would be shown wrong by an allocation at a size other than 0x2C.

structs.name: CMission
structs.comment: **A mission definition** - what `CCountry +0xE40` points at, and the holder of the first of trigger slot 10's two roots: ApplyCountryAIStrategies walks the `CAndTrigger` embedded at `CMission +0xC4` with weight 600. The class has a name string at `+8` and embeds **three** `CAndTrigger`s, of which `+0xC4` is the middle one; which is which was not settled, so no field is declared here. Seven virtual slots, and the slot 6 ApplyCountryAIStrategies calls before the walk takes no arguments and answers a bool. No `size`: the layout past +0x104 was not read.
structs.evidence: The RTTI export gives CMission one vftable at VA 0x15F5D34 (rva 0x11F5D34) with 7 slots and one base, CPersistent at offset 0. The constructor region writes that vftable at VA 0x9C4F99 and inline-constructs three CAndTriggers, one of them at `lea edi,[esi+0xc4]` (VA 0x9C506E); of the 31 code references to the CAndTrigger vftable (rva 0x11B589C) only two neighbourhoods also form a +0xC4 address, and the other is CDecision's, whose +0xC4 write is a CMeanTimeToHappen vftable instead. Declared without a size deliberately. Would be shown wrong by VA 0x9C4F40's body turning out not to be CMission's constructor.

struct_fields.name: id
struct_fields.comment: The province id this entry is about; saved under the key `id` (save token 0xB). The province lists have no hash beside them, so nothing buckets on it.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at construction in AIStrategyList_AddProvinceWeight (0x4A587F) from the key argument, matched on at 0x4A5820, and read by CProvinceValue::SaveContents (rva 0x76BA1) into the `id` key.

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment: The accumulated weight. AIStrategyList_AddProvinceWeight **adds** to it rather than replacing it, deletes the whole entry when the total falls to zero or below, and AIStrategyList_InsertByWeight sorts the list on it descending.
struct_fields.evidence: `add dword ptr [edi+0xc], ebx` at 0x4A5836, the `jle` on the result at 0x4A5890, the `cmp [edx+0xc], eax; jge` sort at 0x4AE652, and CProvinceValue::SaveContents writing it under `value` (save token 0x2A6).

struct_fields.name: tag
struct_fields.comment: Whose entry this is - eight bytes, letters at +8 and the id at +0xC, which is the half the hash buckets on and the half every comparison uses. Saved under the key `id` (save token 0xB), as the letters.
struct_fields.evidence: Both halves written at construction in AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight (0x4A5AC8, 0x4A5ACB) from its two key arguments; `cmp [eax+0xc], ecx` at 0x4A5A93 is the bucket-chain match, the `div` on +0xC at 0x4AE58C is the bucket choice, and CCountryValue::SaveContents takes `strlen(this+8)` for the `id` key.

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment: The accumulated weight. AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight adds to it, removes the entry from both the list and the hash when the total drops below 1, and the list is kept sorted on it descending so that a cap trims the weakest entries.
struct_fields.evidence: `add dword ptr [edi+0x10], ebx` at 0x4A5AFA, `cmp dword ptr [edi+0x10], 1; jge` at 0x4A5AFD, written at construction at 0x4A5ACE, and read by CCountryValue::SaveContents at rva 0x7654A into the `value` key (save token 0x2A6).

struct_fields.name: id
struct_fields.comment: The first half of the pair this entry is keyed by; for CAIStrategy's `building_prov` it is a province id. Saved under the key `id` (save token 0xB).
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [esi+8], edx` in the constructor at 0x4A32F8, matched on at 0x4A593D in AIStrategyList_AddBuildingWeight - which requires **both** this and the string to match - and read by CStringIntInt::SaveContents at rva 0x76E05.

struct_fields.name: key
struct_fields.comment: The second half of the pair, and the only text anywhere in the collector family; for `building_prov` it is a building's name, copied out of the building definition the CHasBuildingTrigger points at. Saved under the key `key` (save token 0xE5), which is what the field is named after.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructed empty at 0x4A32E1-0x4A32EB and then assigned from the constructor's string argument; compared with the string comparison at rva 0x15F70, called from 0x4A596F in the match. Written first by CStringIntInt::SaveContents under save token 0xE5, which ghidra/saveTokens.json gives as `key`. Its 0x1C bytes end exactly where `value` begins at +0x28.

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment: The accumulated weight, at a different offset from the other two payloads' - which is why `building_prov` has a sorted-insert helper of its own (0x4AE700) rather than sharing 0x4AE630.
struct_fields.evidence: `add dword ptr [esi+0x28], edx` at 0x4A5A04, the `jle` on it at 0x4A59F0, and CStringIntInt::SaveContents reading `[edi+0x28]` at rva 0x76E49 into the `value` key.

struct_fields.name: rebuild_tick
struct_fields.comment: **When this strategy was last rebuilt**, as a game tick. CAIStrategy::Rebuild writes `gamestate->tick` (CCurrentGameState +0xBDC) here at 0x4A5D99, four instructions before setting `initialized` at +0x14. The daily gate in RunCountryDailyPass tests `initialized` and `is_static`, not this, so it looks like a diagnostic stamp rather than a cache key - but no scan was run for readers, so that is an impression and not a negative result.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov eax,[eax+0xbdc]; mov [esi+0x10], eax` at 0x4A5D92-0x4A5D99, immediately before `mov byte ptr [esi+0x14], 1`. Would be shown wrong by a writer of +0x10 elsewhere putting something other than a tick there.

struct_fields.name: conquer_prov_count
struct_fields.comment: How many entries `conquer_prov` holds - the `count` of the CList at +0x1C. CAIStrategy::AddConquerProv trims the list from the tail while this exceeds 0x28, or 0x3C when `Personality` is `_AI_MILITARIST_`.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x24], eax` at 0x4A502D and 0x4A5077 against the cap, and `dec dword ptr [esi+0x24]` at 0x4A5063 on each pop. The list head at +0x1C is already recorded, and the engine's CList is {first, last, count, flag} at +0/+4/+8/+0xC.

struct_fields.name: defend_prov_count
struct_fields.comment: The `count` of the `defend_prov` CList at +0x2C. CAIStrategy::AddDefendProv trims while this exceeds 1000.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x34], 0x3e8` at 0x4A5156 and 0x4A51A4, with the matching `dec` in the pop loop.

struct_fields.name: threat_count
struct_fields.comment: The `count` of the `threat` CList at +0x3C. `threat` is the one list of the ten with **no** cap - CAIStrategy::AddThreat does not trim.
struct_fields.evidence: Position from the recorded head at +0x3C and the engine's CList shape, which puts `count` at +8. The absence of a trim is from decoding the whole of 0x4A5240-0x4A525F - eight instructions, no loop.

struct_fields.name: threat_hash_count
struct_fields.comment: How many entries the `threat` hash holds; the first dword of the three-dword hash sub-object at +0x4C, whose `bucket_count` and `buckets` are already recorded at +0x50 and +0x54.
struct_fields.evidence: CAIStrategy::AddThreat passes `this+0x4C` as the hash base to AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight (0x4A5250), which reads bucket_count at hash+4 and buckets at hash+8 - matching the recorded +0x50/+0x54 - and whose insert helper 0x4AE580 does `inc dword ptr [esi]` on hash+0. CAIStrategy::ClearCollectedLists clears the same base at 0x4A3E1E.

struct_fields.name: antagonize_count
struct_fields.comment: The `count` of the `antagonize` CList at +0x58. CAIStrategy::AddAntagonize trims while this exceeds **7**.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x60], 7` at 0x4A5291 and the pop loop's `dec`. The savegame's largest `antagonize` block is exactly 7.

struct_fields.name: antagonize_hash_count
struct_fields.comment: How many entries the `antagonize` hash holds; the first dword of the hash sub-object at +0x68, whose `bucket_count` and `buckets` are already recorded at +0x6C and +0x70.
struct_fields.evidence: CAIStrategy::AddAntagonize passes `this+0x68` as the hash base (0x4A5282), and 0x4AE580's `inc [esi]` is on hash+0 while the recorded +0x6C/+0x70 are hash+4 and hash+8. Cleared at the same base at 0x4A3E33.

struct_fields.name: befriend_count
struct_fields.comment: The `count` of the `befriend` CList at +0x74. CAIStrategy::AddBefriend trims while this exceeds 7, or 14 when `Personality` is `_AI_DIPLOMAT_`.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x7c], eax` at 0x4A545E against the cap computed four instructions earlier. The savegame's largest `befriend` block is exactly 14.

struct_fields.name: befriend_hash_count
struct_fields.comment: How many entries the `befriend` hash holds; first dword of the hash sub-object at +0x84.
struct_fields.evidence: CAIStrategy::AddBefriend passes `this+0x84` as the hash base (0x4A5435) to the helper whose insert does `inc [hash]`; CAIStrategy::ClearCollectedLists clears the same base at 0x4A3E48.

struct_fields.name: befriend_bucket_count
struct_fields.comment: The bucket count of the `befriend` hash - 0x1FF, like every other hash on this class; see +0x50 for the pattern.
struct_fields.evidence: AIStrategyMap_AddCountryWeight divides the country id by `[hash+4]` at 0x4A5A84, reached with the hash base +0x84.

struct_fields.name: mission
struct_fields.comment: **The country's current mission definition**, or null. `CActiveMissionTrigger::Evaluate` (rva 0x5F16D0, the whole of it) is `return scopeCountry->mission == this->+0x40`, so this is the pointer a `mission = X` condition compares against; the saved instance is the separate `active_mission` at +0xE38. ApplyCountryAIStrategies uses it as the **first of trigger slot 10's two roots**: when the mission's own slot 6 answers true it walks the `CAndTrigger` embedded at `CMission +0xC4` with weight 600 and the scope at +0xE44.
struct_fields.evidence: Eight sites in the image touch this displacement through a register. The writer is rva 0xEE76B, which takes it from `[esi+8]` of a record whose `+0xC` and `+0x54` are then copied into this country's +0xE44 and +0xE8C. The class comes from the trigger: `vtable.py --holding` on the body reports exactly one table, CActiveMissionTrigger slot 6, and that body compares `trigger->+0x40` with `country->+0xE40`. CMission is confirmed to embed a CAndTrigger at +0xC4 - of the 31 code references to the CAndTrigger vftable (rva 0x11B589C), only two neighbourhoods also form a +0xC4 address, and the one at rva 0x5C506E is in the function that writes CMission's own vftable at rva 0x5C4F99. Would be shown wrong by a second writer of +0xE40 storing something that is not a CMission*.

struct_fields.name: mission_scope
struct_fields.comment: **The event scope the current mission was started with**, embedded by value - 0x48 bytes, +0xE44 to +0xE8B. It is what ApplyCountryAIStrategies passes as trigger slot 10's `scope` argument when it walks the mission's trigger block, so the mission's conditions are evaluated against the scope the mission was created in rather than against a fresh one. A second scope of the same size follows at +0xE8C.
struct_fields.evidence: Only two sites in the image form this address: rva 0xEE774 and rva 0x4A63D2. The first copies into it from `record+0xC` through rva 0xD4BE0 and immediately afterwards copies `record+0x54` into +0xE8C - the two sources are 0x48 apart and so are the two destinations, which is CEventScope's declared size. The second hands it to slot 10, whose second parameter the record already types `CEventScope*`. The **type is an inference**: rva 0xD4BE0 was not read, so the 0x48 spacing at both ends plus slot 10's parameter type is the whole of the argument. Would be shown wrong by that copy moving something other than 0x48 bytes.

slots_noted: CActiveMissionTrigger slot 6 is recorded because naming that trigger is what identified CCountry +0xE40; vtable.py --holding reports the body in exactly one table, so it is the class's own and not a fold. **Trap 4 is cleared for the whole family with controls on both claimants.** vtable.py --holding over all sixteen bodies in this fragment reports zero tables for every one of them, while the same command on CExistsTrigger's slot-10 body (VA 0x9DABA0) reports one - so the tool was working. And an index of luabind.json's 620 `pointer` values finds none of the sixteen, while finding both known fold cases it should - 0x63D780 (CLicenceTechnologyAction::GetParalell and CFaction::GetNumberOfMembers) and 0x16000 (CDiplomaticAction::GetType and CAIStrategy::GetPersonality). None of the ten adders or the three insert helpers is a virtual or a shared stub, so none takes a slot record.
